decisions.reason: As a broad supplement line with several variants and a clear fit with the firm's consumer-health expansion through pharmacy channels, it is likely to remain in the portfolio.
The skin and hair supplement was clearly launched for pharmacy customers and still fits the firm's established OTC and dietary-supplement positioning, so withdrawal risk is low.
The joint-health supplement supports the firm's portfolio broadening and serves a stable demand area, though its lower prominence makes it somewhat more review-prone than the main lines.

The mushroom-based immune supplement is the most niche and therefore the most vulnerable to rationalization, but it still aligns with the consumer-health strategy and is not yet an obvious candidate for withdrawal.
The OTC migraine triptan strengthens the firm's higher-value pharmacy medicine portfolio and, if still marketed by 2022, would likely be retained unless sales or competitive pressure disappoint.
